# por-glitch internal-node probe -- generated, do not edit

Generated by `sim/por-glitch/control/run_glitch_probe.py`. Re-run it to regenerate this file, the decks under `decks/`, the raw ngspice logs under `logs/` and the traces under `traces/`. The numbers quoted in `design/por_output_chain.md` are transcribed from here, and from nowhere else.

Two PVT points from record `20260801-233813-32fbaa0`, same process/temp, different VDD: `tt_27c_2.97v` (`resetn_post_glitch_v` reads full rail in that record -- 'recovers') and `tt_27c_3.30v` (reads ~0 V -- 'stuck'). Both decks run the identical 300 ns / 0.2 V glitch `../testbench/stimulus.spice` applies, held for 45 ms afterward instead of 26 ms.

## What the numbers say

- At every point, PGDG (the deglitched power-good node) dips well below the
  1.65 V half-rail threshold DURING the 300 ns glitch (minimum column above)
  -- it tracks the collapsing VDD directly, with no RC lag, because
  XMG1/XMG2 are plain ratioed inverters referenced to VDD itself, not to the
  deglitch dwell capacitor CDG (CDG only sits on the POR_RAW input side of
  the chain).
- That transient PGDG fall is enough to fire XMDIS
  (design/por_output_chain.md: "XMDIS slams TIM back to VSS the instant PGDG
  falls"), which is visible in the TIM column: TIM reads near 0 V
  immediately after the glitch ends at every point, i.e. the one-shot has
  been fully discharged by a 300 ns event, not merely disturbed.
- RESETn then regenerates a complete, freshly-timed reset pulse from that
  discharged TIM: one clean low, then release, at both points -- not a
  'stuck' filter. The pulse WIDTH scales with VDD (higher VDD -> longer
  charge to TIM's VDD-referenced trip point, design/por_output_chain.md's
  own "trip is VDD - V_sg" finding), which is why the lower-VDD point's
  pulse completes inside a 5.5 ms observation window and the higher-VDD
  point's does not -- record 20260801-233813-32fbaa0's 'recovers' vs.
  'stuck' split is that window effect, not two different circuit behaviours.
- The crossing count is the read-out for issue #56's OTHER finding. Before
  XMRLK (the release latch DR-016 adds) it was 3, not 2, at both points: the
  regenerated pulse's own release edge carried the same shared-IBIAS release
  chatter sim/por-ramp-rate/control/ root-causes, because a glitch-
  regenerated pulse ends by crossing the same trip detector a cold-start
  release does. With XMRLK it is 1 -- a single clean release rise; the
  pulse's falling edge happens during the glitch itself, before this window
  opens -- so this deck doubles as an independent confirmation that the
  latch fixes the chatter on a release path the ramp-rate testbench never
  exercises.
